messages:
emily: heads up — three customers opened CSAT tickets this morning about alerts firing but Console charts show no matching spike. they all got an ""High error rate"" alert at ~03:14 UTC.
emily: screenshot + sample ticket: https://redwood-internal/attachments/alerts-03-14.png
sahil: can you paste the alert rule + which metric it uses?
emily: alert rule (copied from Console):\n```\nmetric: requests.error_count{service=\"api\"}\naggregation: avg\naggregation_window: 1h\nthreshold: > 0.02\nfor: 5m\n```\nemily: but when I hit ""Evaluate now"" in Console the evaluation shows a 5m window and the value is huge (0.08) — doesn't match the 1h avg shown in the main dashboard.
maria: quick theory: the metrics ingestion rollout last night changed the default rollup to 5m for high-cardinality metrics (PR #2987). dashboards have logic to show 1h rollups but the alert evaluator might be inheriting the new default eval_window = 5m.
metrics-bot: deployment metrics-aggregator v2.11 deployed at 2026-03-17T01:52Z by ci/cd (sha abcdef1) — feature flag "aggregation-default-experiment" enabled in prod.
sahil: if alert eval is using 5m rather than 1h that would explain spikes causing false positives. do we have the evaluator logs? can someone run: `kubectl -n monitoring logs deployment/alert-evaluator --since=1h | grep 1710604800` ?
jordan: on it. repro steps I used: set time window 02:00-04:00 UTC, run the alert query with explicit `window=5m` vs `window=1h` and compare. here's the raw promql emily used: `sum(rate(requests_error_total[5m])) by (service)` — that returns a tall spike at 03:13.
emily: repro steps for support: 1) open ticket console link 2) Evaluate rule now -> shows firing value 3) open chart for same metric with 1h aggregation -> flat 4) run both queries from Console devtools and compare windows.
sahil: confirmed in logs: alert-evaluator request has param `eval_window=5m` for these rules due to aggregator advertising `preferred_window=5m`. that's wrong — alert rules with explicit `aggregation_window: 1h` should override.
maria: digging into PR #2987 — looks like a change to the metric-metadata service where `preferred_window` was promoted to global override when evaluating queries. bug introduced in commit abcdef1 that set precedence wrong.
zach: customers are getting paged. what's the mitigation plan? we need a fast rollback or config patch.
jordan: rolling back metrics-aggregator to v2.10 now, will patch feature flag to disable aggregation-default-experiment. running: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/metrics-aggregator --to-revision=10` — ETA ~6m.
maria: also pushing a hotfix to alert-evaluator to enforce explicit rule window precedence while we audit (small patch, will open PR and promote asap).
sahil: forensics: can we list all alert rules that don't explicitly set aggregation_window? run `curl -s https://metrics-metadata/services | jq '.rules[] | select(.aggregation_window==null) | .id'` and dump to #eng-platform.
emily: I've replied to the three customers: we saw a config rollout that temporarily changed evaluation windows which caused false alerts; we're rolling back and will follow up with RCA. they asked for ETA on full RCA and whether they should silence the alert — I told them we're rolling back now.
jordan: rollback completed at 2026-03-17T02:20Z, monitoring for 30m. alert-evaluator now shows `eval_window=1h` for those rules.
emily: checking tickets — two customers confirmed alerts stopped after rollback. closing one, keeping one open for a final confirmation.
zach: after rollback let's schedule a postmortem + action items: 1) ensure precedence of explicit aggregation_window in evaluator 2) add unit tests for metadata precedence 3) add canary region for aggregator rollout 4) notify customers with RCA.
emily: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @maria pls lead the RCA, @sahil pls add tests, @jordan pls confirm no regressions in next deploy. :thumbsup:
